Week 39 Appendix: A Week of Standoff, Not Collapse

Executive power pushed harder against courts, Congress, and the press this week, but nearly every push met resistance that mostly held.

This week showed a marked acceleration in executive assertion of power under cover of a prolonged government shutdown, combined with an unusually explicit turn toward retaliatory law enforcement and press suppression. The administration used shutdown conditions to conduct mass layoffs of federal workers (including special education and public health staff), redirect appropriated funds without congressional authorization, and threaten Insurrection Act deployment despite repeated judicial rebukes on National Guard deployments to Chicago, Portland, and Los Angeles. Simultaneously, the Pentagon's press credentialing crackdown produced a near-total walkout of mainstream media, DOJ indictments targeted Trump critics (Bolton, implicitly Comey and James), and congressional Republicans amplified rhetoric branding Democrats and "No Kings" protesters as terrorists ahead of a mass nationwide demonstration. A rare public assessment by 340+ former intelligence officials explicitly warned the U.S. is on a trajectory toward "competitive authoritarianism," while courts continued to serve as the primary—if contested and partially overridden—check on executive overreach.
